references: Windows 98 / early-2000s desktop OS (windows, taskbar, IM chat)
summer picnic blanket: gingham cloth, sticker fruit, paper scraps
contemporary acid-print poster: oversized kinetic type, liquid chrome

customReplacement.reason: The PRD explicitly requests a bespoke theme/artifact/behaviour composition system where every atom is drawn in the active world's grammar; upstream component kits contain no window-manager, picnic, or kinetic-poster artifacts, and the ui-library standard says not to add a runtime to a static surface solely for sourcing.

contract.purpose: Every Song Is a Website gives each song its own playable, full-screen visual world assembled from curated themes, artifacts, and light interaction.
contract.canonicalPurpose: Every Song Is a Website gives each song its own playable, full-screen visual world assembled from curated themes, artifacts, and light interaction.
contract.driftNote: New project; no catalog entry yet.
contract.audience: Music fans and web-playful visitors following a shared link.
contract.job: Let a visitor step inside a song's world, play with it for a minute, and jump to the next song.
contract.thesis: Each song is a committed, different world — a 2000s desktop, a picnic blanket, an acid poster — not one layout recoloured. Randomness is confined to position, timing, and surprise; the design is curated.
contract.system: data-theme scoped CSS worlds (desktop/picnic/kinetic) + shared artifact factories + behaviour toolkit (drag, spring, float, trail) + seeded scatter layout + themed chrome and experiment panel.
contract.signature: The theme switcher re-skins every artifact into a different world live — a watermelon becomes a pixel sprite, a window becomes a sticker note.
contract.risk: Full-commit themed worlds risk feeling gimmicky if craft slips; mitigated by restrained motion, authentic surface materials (real gingham, real bevels), and keeping chrome secondary.

ownerFeedback.note: Owner supplied the complete direction in the PRD: three named worlds with era, mood, artifacts, and interactions specified.
